reference.title: Heel Walk
reference.listing: Page could not be read here (gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy); the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice.

prescription.frequency: 3-4 times a week (warm-up or shin conditioning)
prescription.progression: Longer distance, then toes turned in and out, then a light weight in the hands

cues.text: Stand tall, hands on the hips. Pull the toes and the balls of the feet up off the floor.
Walk forward on the heels with short steps, toes up the whole time.
Stand tall; do not sit back or bend forward at the hips.
Bring the feet together and lower the toes.

mistakes.mistake: Sitting the hips back to stay on the heels
mistakes.fix: Stand tall, hips over the feet; take shorter steps.
Keep pulling the toes up the whole time.

kinematics.norm: Dorsiflexed so only the heel touches, about 15-25 degrees (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #22395, Heel Walk, video (movement reference; page not readable here)
Docherty et al. 2005, Functional-performance deficits in volunteers with functional ankle instability (J Athl Train)

cautions: Stop if you feel sharp, radiating or nerve-type pain.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Shin pain (for example shin splints): keep sets short and stop if it gets worse.
Walk on a flat, clear surface; near a wall if your balance is unsure.
modify: March in place on the heels.
regressions: Seated or standing toe raises (heels down, toes up).
Marching in place on the heels.
progressions: A light dumbbell in each hand.

muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Holds the pelvis level over each stance leg (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Holds the pelvis level over each stance leg (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.quads_r: Keep the knees nearly straight so each step lands on the heel (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Keep the knees nearly straight so each step lands on the heel (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_r: Swing each leg through with the toes held up (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_l: Swing each leg through with the toes held up (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.calves_r: The calves lengthen as the toes are pulled up. The main movers, tibialis anterior and the toe extensors on the front of the shin, are not separate regions on this rig, so they do not glow (heel walking is a standard test and strengthening drill for the ankle dorsiflexors).
muscleNotes.calves_l: The calves lengthen as the toes are pulled up. The main movers, tibialis anterior and the toe extensors on the front of the shin, are not separate regions on this rig, so they do not glow.
